# Notes of this project for coding agents

Issue assistant: A GitHub Action that looks after issues: a first analysis by an AI that only reads, labels, duplicates and reminders, all checked before posting.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- The action is defined in `action.yml` and runs the package `issue_assistant/`, with `python3 -m issue_assistant`. `docs/architecture/modules.md` has the map of its modules: each imports only from those before it in `issue_assistant/__init__.py`, which hands on all their names, as `assistant.render_analysis` in the tests. A test that replaces a name does so in the module that looks it up, as `monkeypatch.setattr(assistant.cli, "GitHub", …)`, or with `replace_everywhere` of `tests/support.py` when several do; `tests/test_package.py` checks the layers, the length of modules and functions, and that only the standard library is imported.
- `README.md` gives the overview with a line and a link for each feature, the pages of `docs/` hold the details and are the website, with a page for each feature in `docs/features/`, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- The tests are in `tests/`; `scripts/check.sh` runs every check.
- The weekly Mutation workflow runs the tests in mutmut's copy, `mutants/`, where each module of `issue_assistant/` holds every mutant beside its function. A test that reads the code as text, with `package_source()` of `tests/support.py`, `read_text()`, `open()` or `inspect.getsource()`, can't pass there and gets `@pytest.mark.mutation_unsafe`; a check of behaviour that it makes as well goes into a test of its own. `tests/test_mutation_safety.py` finds each unmarked one that reads it in its own module; it doesn't follow helpers of `conftest.py` or `support.py`, so keep such reads out of them. The help of the commands and options lives in the tables `SCRIPT_COMMANDS` and `SCRIPT_OPTIONS`, and `main()` hands each command to a function of its own: mutmut copies a whole function for each of its mutants, and leaves the constants of a module alone.
- The Action test, `.github/workflows/action-test.yml`, runs the action as its users run it. Each of its jobs ends with the step *Explain the failure*, and each step of a job belongs to a part that the PR coach explains from `.github/checks.project.toml`; a new job, step or part comes with its explanation, which `tests/test_coach.py` checks.
- The Workflow test, `.github/workflows/workflow-test.yml`, calls every reusable workflow as a dry run, and its job *reusable workflows*, a required check, reads the jobs of its run with `scripts/workflow_test.py`. A renamed job of a reusable workflow, or a renamed step that writes the plan of a dry run, goes into `CALLS` of that script in the same pull request; `tests/test_workflow_test.py` checks it. Every job of a reusable workflow starts its checkouts with the guard that stops it when GitHub names no commit of the workflow, which `tests/test_templates.py` keeps in each.
- The tests of `tests/test_templates.py` that walk the workflows for pins, checkouts and scripts check the templates and the workflows of this project alone, and leave those that `.github/blueprint/owned.txt` lists to the blueprint, whose tests hold the same rules for them in every repository (Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint#697). So an update of the blueprint that changes one of its workflows, such as the screenshot bot, needs no change of these tests, and a rule that a workflow of the blueprint should follow goes into the blueprint's tests. A rule of a name of this project, such as its inputs `canary` and `smoke`, still checks every workflow.
- The Evaluate workflow, `.github/workflows/evaluate.yml`, measures the accuracy by hand and brings it to `docs/accuracy.md`: its job `replay` runs `evaluate` with the AI, and its job `publish`, without one, the command `accuracy-page`, which writes only between the lines `<!-- accuracy numbers: start -->` and `<!-- accuracy numbers: end -->`. A change of the head of a report in `render_evaluation` goes into `REPORT` as well, since `publish` refuses a report that doesn't fit; `tests/test_evaluate.py` checks that the two fit. It runs only on `main`, where its secrets are, so no pull request runs it.
- GitHub runs only its own actions and those that `[actions.selected]` of `.github/repository.toml` lists. A new action that only the workflows of this project run, such as an action of a new engine, goes into `patterns_allowed` of `[actions.selected]` in `.github/repository.project.toml`, in the same pull request; `tests/test_repository_settings.py` checks it, and the settings bot fails on `main` without it. An action that such an action only runs in turn goes there too, and into `RUN_IN_TURN` of that test.
- The pictures in `docs/images` show what the assistant posts: `scripts/images/pages.py` builds their pages from its texts, and `bash scripts/render-images.sh` takes them, with Docker, and writes `scripts/images/manifest.json`. A change of a text of `locales/`, of the cleaning, of a page or of `scripts/images/style.css` that a picture shows fails `test_the_pictures_show_what_the_assistant_posts` until you run the script and commit the pictures and the manifest; the screenshot bot renders them anew after a new version of the tools.
- A new REST request of the package has to be in GitHub's OpenAPI description, whose copy is `tests/github/api.github.com.json`, and in a form that `tests/test_rest_contract.py` can read from the source: a string or an f-string, built in the function that sends it. `scripts/github_schemas.py` writes the copies; the job `schema-refresh` of the Action test brings new ones by itself, so don't refresh them in a pull request that has no other reason to.
- Every `gh api` asks for `API_VERSION_HEADER` of `issue_assistant/github.py`, also those of `scripts/` and of the workflows of this project alone. A script starts `gh` at one place, with `--header` and the header as its last arguments; one that its job checks out alone, such as `scripts/canary_queue.py`, keeps a copy of the header. A step of a workflow that calls `gh api` has `API_VERSION_HEADER` in its environment and writes `gh api --header "$API_VERSION_HEADER"`. `tests/test_rest_contract.py` fails on a call without it and on a step whose header differs, and the tests of a script on a copy that differs, so a change of the version changes every copy.
- Every job of a workflow of this project that blocks with Harden-Runner, those of the reusable workflows above all, runs the steps of the blueprint's jobs that block: *Let Harden-Runner see the DNS lookups* where it keeps sudo, then *Make sure that Harden-Runner blocks* with the id `blocks` and the very script of the blueprint's workflows, then the warm-up; a later step that runs on `always()`, `failure()` or `!cancelled()` also has `steps.blocks.outcome != 'failure'`, or `steps.blocks.outcome == 'success'` in a job that lets Harden-Runner see the DNS lookups first (decision 0029). An update of the blueprint that changes the script of that step fails `tests/test_templates.py` until the copies here take the new one.
